usual_baseline: Guideline-compliant prescribing in 35–76%. Indication and duration documented in 55.88–89%; review or stop dates as low as 17%. In one surgical clinic 71% of renal stone patients got antibiotics they did not need [1992]. Prophylactic prescriptions had no indication or duration recorded [1920].
fix_that_works: Weekly microbiology-led ward rounds plus teaching: Microguide compliance 53% to 83% [1896]. Adding electronic prescribing that forces fields: review/stop dates 17% to 100%, indications 78% to 96%, IV duration 63% to 93% [1995]. QR-code posters and teaching: initial choice 59% to 82% [2780].
fix_that_fails: Posters and a talk gave modest gains: adherence 65% to 72% [1923]. In urology, discharge choice stayed at 61% and composite compliance only 43% to 53%, with 48% unjustified deviations [2780]. One unit reported improvement with no figures [2230].
consultant_advice: Commonly done and the fix is known: a prompt in the prescribing system plus microbiology on the ward. Don't just measure documentation of indication. Audit appropriateness of discharge antibiotics, prophylactic courses, or antibiotics in conditions where none are needed, such as renal colic.
